descriptionChirho: A Roman silver coin worth approximately one day's wages for a common laborer, used as both a unit of currency and a measure of economic value in NT narratives and parables. The singular and plural forms represent the same monetary referent with no semantic distinction. Multilingual glosses consistently transliterate or directly borrow the term: Spanish 'denario/denarios,' Arabic 'دينار/دِينَار' (dinar, a cognate loanword), Hindi 'दीनार' (dinar), Korean '데나리온' (denarion, transliteration), Swahili 'dinari' (dinar). Occurrences include the parable of the workers paid a denarius (Matt 20:2, 9-10, 13), the tribute coin shown to Jesus (Matt 22:19; Mark 12:15), the parable of the unforgiving servant (Matt 18:28), the cost of feeding the 5,000 (Mark 6:37; John 6:7), and the anointing at Bethany (Mark 14:5; John 12:5).
